To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the symmetry groups of a system are determined by the properties of the set of its solutions and by the existence of a large number (at least three) of nondegenerate periodic solutions.
the symmetry group of an autonomous dynamical system is trivial if the system has a large number of periodic solutions or if its asymptotic surfaces are transversally intersecting.
the symmetry groups of a system are determined by the structure of its phase fluxes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the existence and properties of symmetry groups of dynamic equations.
a generalization of the concept of a symmetry group of a dynamic system.
the following questions: (i) What are the necessary and sufficient conditions for a system to possess a symmetry group?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the equations of motion of a heavy asymmetric body with a fixed centre of mass do not possess any non-trivial symmetry.
the symmetry group of a dynamic system is not an invariant of its qualitative type, and is determined by the specific properties of its phase space.
the symmetry groups of a Hamiltonian system are determined by the structure of the phase space of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem of the existence of a non-trivial analytic symmetry group of a dynamic system has been solved in a complete manner.
the existence of a symmetry group is a very rare event.
the existence of a non-trivial group of phase fluxes of a system, in the sense of the above, is a rare phenomenon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the existence of a large number (at least 2n − 3) of nondegenerate periodic solutions is an obstacle to the existence of a nontrivial symmetry group of a system.
symmetry groups of dynamic system play an important part both in the qualitative theory of differential equations and in perturbation theory.

the presence of symmetry groups of the system of equations under study can significantly simplify the solution process and, in some cases, even make the problem of finding a complete solution solvable.
